messages.subject: Problem with the "wordcount" example
parts:
Hi all!
I tried to do the wordcount example from Jeffrey Breen's tutorial. However, it doesn't work properly. I think the problem is that R or rmr isn't reading the right data-file.

In the tutorial it says that I need to populate the hdfs.sh.
Currently this file lies in the following directory: /home/cloudera/TutorialBreen/bin   Do I have to change this or can I execute "#!/bin/sh" or even "/home/cloudera/TutorialBreen/bin/sh"?

After that it should create the following directory: /home/cloudera/airline/data .... In my Terminal it says it created the file but when I check it in my cloudera-folder, there is no airline folder. And neither there is any data which should be there after I executed: /usr/bin/hadoop fs -put data/hadoop/wordcount/* /user/cloudera/wordcount/data
The data is in the folder /home/cloudera/TutorialBreen/data/hadoop/airline
Do I have to link or move this .csv File to another directory? Because when I finished all the R commands there is no result at the moment: I always get the following errors:

> colnames(df) = c('word', 'count')
Error in `colnames<-`(`*tmp*`, value = c("word", "count")) :
  'names' attribute [2] must be the same length as the vector [0]
> df = df[order(-df!$count),]
Error: unexpected '!' in "df = df[order(-df!"
> df = df[order(-df$count),]
Error in -df$count : invalid argument to unary operator
> print(head(df))
data frame with 0 columns and 0 rows

My guess is that something is not right with the reading of the datafile (probably fals directory) as the commands are the same as in the tutorial and there fore should be ok.

If someone could help me I would be very thankful!

Thanks
Roman
